references.text: The context of this verse is where Gideon asks about the men who were killed at Tabor, who were his brothers
A similar oath formula 'as Pharaoh lives' is used here as a parallel to 'as the Lord lives'
Saul uses the same oath formula 'as the Lord lives' when he makes a solemn oath
David uses the oath 'as the Lord lives' to confirm the truth of what he says
David uses the oath 'as the Lord, the God of Israel, lives' in connection with sparing or taking life
The oath 'as the Lord lives' is used in the context of vengeance and justice
Abimelech kills his seventy brothers as a contrast to Gideon's right to blood vengeance for his brothers
The law of blood vengeance and retribution for murder, which underlies Gideon's action
